Role Summary
The AI Process Transformation Lead will help Global Distribution teams fundamentally improve how work gets done by combining deep process understanding with the opportunities created by artificial intelligence.

As a senior member of a dedicated Implementation Pod, this role will work directly alongside the business team, Applied AI Solutions Lead, and AI Adoption & Integration Lead during focused engagements. The AI Process Transformation Lead will rapidly develop a fact-based understanding of the current workflow, identify the highest-value points of leverage, and co-design a materially better future state.

The role requires someone who can quickly make sense of complex and unfamiliar work: understanding activities, volumes, decisions, handoffs, exceptions, controls, systems, and performance, while challenging assumptions about what can be a candidate for change.

This is not a traditional requirements-gathering or business-analysis position. The AI Process Transformation Lead is a senior transformation practitioner who helps the business reimagine its work and stays deeply engaged through implementation.

Responsibilities
Understand the Work:
- Rapidly get to the core of how a business workflow operates today through direct engagement with the Associates and leaders who perform and manage the work.
- Map the critical activities, inputs, outputs, volumes, decisions, handoffs, systems, controls, exceptions, bottlenecks, and recurring sources of effort or friction.
- Establish practical performance baselines and identify the portions of the workflow where improvement could create meaningful business value.
- Distinguish root causes from symptoms and challenge assumptions about why existing activities, approvals, or handoffs exist.

Reimagine the Work:
- Co-design the target-state workflow alongside the business team and Applied AI Solutions Lead, combining deep knowledge of how the work operates today with emerging AI capabilities to create a materially better future state.
- Determine which elements of the workflow should be simplified, eliminated, automated, AI-augmented, or fundamentally reimagined.
- Translate the future-state design into clear roles, decisions, handoffs, exception paths, controls, and measures of success.
- Maintain a strong focus on the primary business outcome and resist unnecessary complexity or scope expansion.

Deliver and Learn at Pace:
- Stay actively involved through rapid build, testing, iteration, launch, and handoff rather than treating process design as a front-end deliverable.
- Work with real users to test the proposed future state and adapt the workflow as the team learns what works in practice.
- Partner with the AI Adoption & Integration Lead to ensure the redesigned process can be understood, adopted, and sustained by the business.
- Capture reusable process patterns and lessons that can accelerate future engagements or identify opportunities for broader transformation.

Mindset
- Analytical and structured: naturally seeks facts, patterns, clarity, and measurable evidence.
- Organized and grounded: quickly turns messy work into an understandable operating model.
- Insatiably curious about how work actually happens.
- Comfortable getting into operational detail without losing sight of the business outcome.
- Challenges legacy assumptions respectfully and constructively.
- AI-forward, while remaining focused on solving the problem rather than forcing AI into it.
- High urgency, low ego, and energized by solving a succession of different business problems as part of a team.

Qualifications
Required:
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in business, operations, engineering, finance, information systems, or a related discipline and 8+ years of related experience.
- Experience in process transformation, operations, management consulting, continuous improvement, business architecture, or related roles.
- Demonstrated experience independently leading the analysis and redesign of complex business workflows.
- Strong quantitative and analytical skills, including experience establishing performance baselines and measurable target outcomes.
- Ability to rapidly learn unfamiliar business domains and ask incisive questions of subject-matter experts.
- Strong facilitation and stakeholder-management skills across frontline, management, and senior-leadership audiences.
- Working understanding of generative AI, automation, and emerging AI-enabled workflows.

Preferred:
- Experience in asset management, financial services, or another regulated environment.
- Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, process engineering, service design, or related disciplines.
- Experience implementing technology-enabled transformation rather than only developing recommendations.
- Familiarity with process-mapping, process-mining, workflow, or analytical tools.

The team works collaboratively with investment professionals as governance considerations are evaluated alongside other factors within T. Rowe Price’s active investment process.

Role Summary
The T. Rowe Price internship program includes a formal orientation, peer and senior mentor assignments, and formal learning opportunities. In addition to work assignments within the Corporate Governance team, interns gain exposure to associates and senior leaders across the firm through an executive speaker series, networking and social events, and engagement with our Business Resource Groups.

During the 10-week program in Baltimore, the Corporate Governance Intern will support the development of a research paper that sets out the value of corporate governance within the active management investment process. The paper may reflect relevant academic research as well as insights gained from T. Rowe Price investment teams.

This opportunity is well suited for a student who enjoys research, writing, critical thinking, and exploring the connection between corporate governance and investing.

Responsibilities
Responsibilities may include:
- Support the development of a research paper examining the value of corporate governance within the active management investment process
- Conduct and synthesize relevant academic and other research
- Analyze information from multiple sources to identify key themes and findings
- Develop clear, well-supported written analysis based on research findings
- Contribute to research

Qualifications
Required:
- Full-time student pursuing a bachelor’s degree with an expected graduation date of December 2028 through May/June 2029
- Open to all majors
- Strong research, analytical, and written communication skills
- Ability to evaluate information from multiple sources and develop well-supported conclusions
- Intellectual curiosity and interest in understanding the relationship between corporate governance, companies, and investing

Preferred:
- Cumulative grade point average of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale
- Coursework or experience in areas such as political science, public policy, legal research, humanities, economics, business, finance, or related fields
- Experience conducting research or producing substantive written analysis
- Strong critical thinking skills and attention to detail
- Interest in corporate governance and investment management

Role Summary
We are seeking a Senior Manager, Technology & Cyber Risk Management, to join the AI, Model and Technology risk team in the Chief Risk Officer organization. This second-line role provides independent oversight and credible challenges of technology, cyber, cloud, data, third-party, resilience, and AI-related risks across the enterprise. The role partners with technology, cybersecurity, business, compliance, operational risk, legal, and internal audit stakeholders to ensure risks are identified, assessed, monitored, reported, and managed in line with enterprise risk appetite and regulatory expectations.

Responsibilities
- Provide second-line oversight and credible challenge to management of technology, cyber, cloud, resilience, third-party technology, data protection, and AI-related risks across the enterprise.
- Lead and support risk assessments, control reviews, thematic deep dives, and oversight of major technology change, cyber, and AI-enabled initiatives.
- Lead or support AI, model & technology incident management program ensuring timely identification, reporting, escalation, root cause analysis, remediation and lessons learned for technology, cyber, data and AI incidents.
- Assess whether risks, controls, remediation plans, exceptions, and risk acceptances are appropriately identified, challenged, escalated, and managed.
- Develop risk reporting, KRIs, dashboards, and committee materials that provide senior leaders with clear insight into technology, cyber, and AI risk trends.
- Support enhancements to technology, cyber, and AI risk frameworks, policies, standards control frameworks, assessment methodologies, and governance routines, including alignment to recognized AI governance and GenAI security frameworks.
- Monitor regulatory developments, industry guidance, threat trends, audit findings, incidents, and emerging technology risks to inform second-line oversight priorities.
- Collaborate with Technology, Cybersecurity, Compliance, Operational Risk, Third-Party Risk, Business Resilience, Legal, and Internal Audit to drive consistent risk coverage and effective remediation.
- Partner with business risk managers to support broader technology, data, and operations business risk initiatives

Business knowledge
- Strong understanding of the three-lines-of-defense model and the role of a second-line risk function in oversight, challenge, aggregation, and reporting.
- Understanding of enterprise risk and business risk domains, and demonstrated success of integrating technology & cyber risk management activities into overall business unit and enterprise risk management plans
- Knowledge of technology and cyber risk domains, including information security, cloud, infrastructure, application security, data protection, resilience, incident management, third-party technology risk, identity and access management, and AI risk management.
- Understanding of financial services regulatory expectations related to technology, cyber, operational resilience, third-party risk, data governance, and AI/model risk intersections.
- Familiarity with risk and control frameworks such as NIST CSF 2.0, NIST 800-53, ISO 27001/27002, COBIT, COSO, FFIEC guidance, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 23894, SR 11-7 model risk management guidance, and OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications.
